To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a continuous definition of conditional probabilities p (n) k|i in the tree is better than a discrete one and that (2) a tree structure is better than a linear structure.

• The discrete definition of conditional probabilities is a special case of the continuous one, • The continuous definition of conditional probabilities can be applied to any tree structure and any type of features, and • The continuous definition is a natural generalization of the discrete one, as it allows to use the same tree structure and the same feature space as in the discrete case.
• The tree-based models for classification are a good fit for the extreme classification task.
